Poppy Seed Cake

Served at: Noaptea Lupilor

Serves 8Prep 20 minCook 45 min

Poppy Seed Cake is a traditional dessert often enjoyed during Noaptea Lupilor, a festival that celebrates the mystical and natural world. This moist, nutty cake is infused with ground poppy seeds, symbolizing fertility and prosperity, making it a meaningful treat for the occasion.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (120 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) milk
  • 1/3 cup (45 g) ground poppy seeds
  • 1/4 cup (60 g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1/4 tsp salt
  • Powdered sugar for dusting (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour an 8-inch (20 cm) round cake pan.
  2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, ground poppy seeds, baking powder, and salt.
  3. In a separate large bowl, beat the eggs and sugar until pale and fluffy.
  4. Add the melted butter, milk, and vanilla extract to the egg mixture and mix well.
  5. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, folding gently until combined.
  6. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan and smooth the top.
  7. Bake for 40-45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
  8. Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
  9. Dust with powdered sugar before serving, if desired.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, substitute half the milk with sour cream or yogurt.
  • Toast the poppy seeds lightly before grinding to enhance their nuttiness.
  • Serve with a dollop of whipped cream or a drizzle of honey for added sweetness.
